extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners seeking Knight Foundation funding or interested in Knight-funded research (e.g., academics, policy analysts, journalists, nonprofit program staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the thematic priorities and expectations Knight Foundation uses when commissioning research — the kinds of topics and public-interest aims research should advance. Useful for prospective grantees or collaborators planning work aligned with Knight's agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to understanding of informed and engaged communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight commissions research that contributes to the broader understanding of informed and engaged communities, both now and in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioned research should advance knowledge about how communities obtain information, participate civically, and sustain engagement over time. Projects should tie into ongoing conversations of significance to the foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align with key thematic areas of significance to the foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Our commissioned research has focused on key thematic areas that contribute to ongoing conversations of significance to the foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and projects should target Knight's priority themes (see series/topics listed on the page) rather than unrelated topics; alignment with those themes will be a primary organizing consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pew–Knight Initiative focus: civic information, belief formation, and civic engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research under the Pew–Knight Initiative seeks to deepen understanding of how Americans absorb civic information, form beliefs and identities, and engage in their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should investigate information flows, belief/identity formation processes, and civic engagement behaviors in ways that inform policy, practice, or public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free expression and First Amendment research priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight Foundation values the First Amendment, evident in ongoing research on free expression (Knight Free Expression Research Series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that examine speech, campus expression, book restrictions, and related First Amendment questions are within scope; historical continuity (research since 2004) suggests preference for rigorous, longitudinal, or comparative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of asset managers and transparency in investment practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight publishes research to foster transparency about the use of diverse owned asset managers and to improve institutional investment practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research proposals should support transparency, measurement, or reforms around manager diversity (examples include higher education endowments). Outputs that inform institutional change or public accountability are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust, media, and democracy research priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight (with partners) studies media trust, news sustainability, and attitudes toward internet policy and technology (Trust, Media and Democracy series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred research topics include public trust in media, business models for journalism sustainability, and public attitudes toward platform governance and internet policy; work that produces actionable insights for media ecosystems is valued.
